requirement: Describe the study as a multicenter two-phase behavioral trial: an open-label smoking-cessation phase followed by randomization of abstinent participants to three parallel lifestyle conditions.

evidence.text: The study first provides smoking cessation and then randomizes abstinent participants among three lifestyle conditions.

notes: Only Phase 2 is randomized; do not describe all enrolled smokers as randomized.

requirement: Name the randomized conditions as Blood Pressure Control, Weight Gain Prevention, and Usual Lifestyle/self-help materials, with ongoing primary-care blood-pressure management continuing in all groups.

evidence.text: Participants are assigned to BPC, WGP, or Usual Lifestyle and continue usual primary-care management.

notes: The usual-lifestyle arm is the common control for the two planned contrasts.

requirement: Represent the planned randomized allocation as equal across the three groups, based on 190 planned participants per group before attrition.

evidence.text: The attrition plan shows 570 randomized as 190, 190, and 190 across the three groups.

notes: The ratio is derived from the equal group counts rather than stated as a randomization ratio.

requirement: Ask for the sequence-generation, allocation-concealment, blocking, and any randomization-stratification details before finalizing the randomization section.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering randomization implementation

evidence.text: The protocol states random assignment to three conditions but does not specify the sequence-generation or concealment method.

notes: Do not invent a centralized system, block size, or stratification factors.

requirement: Distinguish the planned 1,267 Phase 1 enrollees, 570 randomized participants, and effective primary-analysis sample of 435 or 145 per arm after assumed 10% attrition and 15% smoking relapse.

evidence.text: The plan enrolls 1267, randomizes 570, and targets 435 abstinent completers, 145 per group, after attrition and relapse.

notes: Do not report the effective analysis sample as the total randomized sample.

requirement: Define the primary efficacy outcomes as change in blood pressure and change in body weight from baseline to the one-year follow-up among participants who remain abstinent from smoking.

evidence.text: Primary endpoints are changes in BP and body weight among abstinent smokers at one year.

notes: Experts should decide whether SBP and DBP are separate primary variables within the BP endpoint family.

requirement: Anchor the primary analysis to 12 months post-cessation and treat the six-month assessment as an additional, non-primary analysis timepoint.

evidence.text: Follow-up visits occur at six and 12 months post cessation; the primary analysis is at one year.

notes: Do not promote the six-month result to a co-primary timepoint.

requirement: Define the primary efficacy analysis set as randomized participants who have not relapsed to smoking and who provide follow-up outcome data.

evidence.text: Primary analyses are restricted to randomized participants with prolonged abstinence and available follow-up data.

notes: This is not a conventional all-randomized ITT analysis and must be labelled transparently.

requirement: Use the abstinent-completer population for the primary efficacy analysis and repeat the treatment comparisons secondarily using all randomized participants.

evidence.text: The primary analysis is restricted to abstinent participants with data; a secondary analysis uses all participants.

notes: The all-participant analysis must not be presented as the protocol primary analysis.

requirement: Explicitly identify that the primary effect is conditional on post-randomization smoking abstinence and available outcomes, and ask the statistician to confirm the intended estimand and interpretation under relapse and loss to follow-up.
acceptable_values: conditional effect among abstinent observed participants
specific question about post-randomization selection and target population

evidence.text: The protocol conditions the primary analysis on no relapse and observed follow-up data, both post-randomization quantities.

notes: Do not describe this analysis as an unconditional treatment-policy estimand or ordinary ITT effect.

requirement: Analyze each one-year continuous primary outcome using ANCOVA with treatment group, the corresponding baseline outcome value, and study site, and estimate active-versus-control contrasts.

evidence.text: Primary outcomes use ANCOVA adjusted for baseline outcome and site, with each experimental group compared with UL.

notes: Any additional imbalance-selected covariates are addressed separately.

requirement: Record the protocol rule that baseline variables found to differ significantly between groups are added as covariates, and require the final SAP to predefine the screening test, threshold, and eligible covariate set.

evidence.text: ANCOVA adjusts for baseline variables found to differ significantly between groups, but the screening implementation is not specified.

notes: The protocol rule is explicit but not executable without operational detail.

requirement: Define the two planned treatment contrasts for every primary outcome as Blood Pressure Control versus Usual Lifestyle and Weight Gain Prevention versus Usual Lifestyle; no BPC-versus-WGP confirmatory contrast is specified.
acceptable_values: no required BPC versus WGP contrast

evidence.text: Each of the two experimental groups is compared to the UL group.

notes: Direction of benefit depends on the outcome: lower BP and less weight gain are favorable.

requirement: For the two active-versus-UL comparisons within an outcome, use the documented protected Fisher LSD structure: first test an omnibus equality-of-means hypothesis and perform pairwise contrasts only if that test rejects.
acceptable_values: pairwise tests only after omnibus rejection

evidence.text: Fisher LSD is used with an initial omnibus test gating subsequent pairwise comparisons.

notes: This requirement captures the stated within-outcome comparison gate, not control across distinct primary outcomes.

requirement: Ask the statistician to reconcile the Fisher-LSD analysis text with sample-size calculations using two-sided alpha 0.025, and to state the alpha used for the omnibus and pairwise tests.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering omnibus alpha, pairwise alpha, and relationship to 0.025 planning alpha

evidence.text: The analysis specifies Fisher LSD, while the power tables repeatedly use a two-sided alpha=0.025 test.

notes: Do not silently choose alpha 0.05 or 0.025 for the final confirmatory tests.

requirement: Ask whether success requires findings for blood pressure, body weight, both, or any selected contrast, and whether SBP and DBP are separate members of the primary family.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering endpoint family, contrast family, and overall success rule

evidence.text: The protocol names blood pressure and body weight as primary endpoints but does not define a joint study-level success rule.

notes: A generated SAP must not invent a conjunctive or disjunctive rule.

requirement: State that participants who discontinue are classified as smoking relapses for smoking-status analyses, while primary BP/weight analyses use available outcomes, and ask for an operational strategy for missing one-year BP and weight values.

evidence.text: Discontinuers are assumed to have relapsed, but the continuous primary analyses are restricted to those with available follow-up data.

notes: Smoking-status imputation does not itself impute BP or body weight.

requirement: Include servings of fruits and vegetables, dietary fat intake, overnight urinary chloride excretion, and self-reported physical activity as secondary endpoints, analyzed using ANCOVA analogous to the primary outcomes.

evidence.text: The four secondary endpoints use ANCOVA with baseline, site, and any selected baseline variables.

notes: These outcomes are not primary endpoints.

requirement: Define smoking relapse as tobacco use on seven consecutive days or on at least one day per week for two consecutive weeks; set relapse date to the first tobacco-use day in the qualifying interval.
acceptable_values: at least 1 day/week for 2 consecutive weeks
first use day is event date

evidence.text: Relapse and its event date are explicitly defined using the seven-day or two-week criteria.

notes: This derived event supports the exploratory time-to-relapse analysis.

requirement: Analyze exploratory time to smoking relapse with Cox proportional-hazards regression using intervention group, assign discontinuers without prior relapse an event on the day after their last visit, and censor non-relapsers at the one-year visit.
acceptable_values: discontinuer event day after last visit

evidence.text: Time to relapse uses Cox regression; discontinuers are assigned relapse after last visit and non-relapsers are censored at one year.

notes: This is exploratory and should not be included in the primary multiplicity family without a decision update.

requirement: For the open-label Phase 1 cessation component, define prolonged abstinence at session 4 as no tobacco, not even a puff, for 14 days confirmed by expired CO below 10 ppm; count discontinuers as smoking and report a proportion with 95% CI.

evidence.text: Phase 1 prolonged abstinence is 14 days with CO confirmation; discontinuers are smoking and the rate receives a 95% CI.

notes: The optional logistic-regression predictors are exploratory.

requirement: Carry forward collection of serious adverse events, nicotine-replacement side effects, and relevant safety observations, but ask for the final safety analysis population, treatment-emergent window, coding dictionary, and tabulation rules.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering safety population, window, coding, and summaries

evidence.text: The protocol describes repeated SAE and side-effect monitoring but does not provide a statistical safety-summary specification.

notes: Do not invent MedDRA version or an as-treated safety set.

requirement: Describe independent DSMB review of baseline, outcome, safety, and enrollment summaries at least twice yearly, without inventing formal efficacy or futility boundaries.

evidence.text: An external DSMB reviews aggregate study data at least twice annually and may recommend early stoppage.

notes: The protocol provides monitoring governance but no alpha-spending or stopping rule.
